**Scope:** draft — persistent terminal panes: a new `PersistentPty` core service that talks to an external `opencode-pty` sidecar daemon (protocol v4, companion Rust runtime in a separate repo) over a Unix socket with token auth, plus TUI pane workspace/layout components, server handlers with short-lived connect tickets, and regenerated client surfaces.

- The durability design is coherent: terminals outlive the opencode process via a detached daemon; authoritative snapshots + resize checkpoints + offset-based replay give multi-client consistency; controller delivery is lossless while observers get bounded delivery — the right trade-off, and stale sidecar registrations are recovered rather than trusted.
- Security layering is mostly sound (per-uid runtime dir keyed by hashed DB path, token-on-first-frame over the socket, ping validation of instance_id/pid/protocol before reuse, 8MB frame cap). **Please clarify the constant-header check** in the server handler: rejecting requests whose `PTY_CONNECT_TOKEN_HEADER` doesn't equal a compile-time constant value is not authentication by itself — confirm real authorization flows through the session auth + short-lived ticket, and document what that header actually defends against.
- Operational questions a maintainer will want answered before this leaves draft:
  - Orphan lifecycle: the daemon is spawned detached/unref'd and intentionally survives service restarts; only explicit stop/restart tears it down. What's the user-facing story for "why is there an opencode-pty process running" / cleanup after uninstall?
  - Portability: `net.createConnection(registration.socket)` assumes AF_UNIX; Windows needs a named-pipe path or an explicit unsupported-platform gate.
  - Cross-repo coupling: merging requires a released protocol-v4 sidecar; `UnavailableError` suggests graceful degradation, but the TUI entry points should be hidden (not just erroring) when the binary is absent.
- Verification hygiene is good: typecheck per package, sidecar tests gated behind `OPENCODE_PTY_BIN`, cargo test/clippy on the companion, and generated client files regenerated rather than hand-edited.

Same file, but a different bug and a different fix. I tested the fix from #42162 and #42233, which is spawning the helper detached so it gets its own process group. It does not fix this.

current behaviour: pipe stdout, not detached      HUNG       5007ms
#42233 proposal:   pipe stdout, detached: true    HUNG       5007ms
this issue's fix:  stdout ignored, not detached   resolved   4ms
both together                                    resolved   3ms

#42162 is about the provider being suspended. Ctrl-Z sends SIGTSTP to the whole foreground group, the forked wl-copy stops with it, and other programs then hang trying to paste from a stopped selection owner.

This one needs no Ctrl-Z and no signals. A plain copy is enough. The forked helper is running fine and the clipboard works. What hangs is opencode's own clipboard.write(), because the helper inherited the stdout pipe and close waits for stdio to close as well as for the process to exit.

detached: true gives the child its own process group but does not close the stdout it already inherited, which is why it makes no difference here. Both are worth fixing and neither fix covers the other.

Ran into this on Windows ARM64 too. The official ARM64 build is compiled with a Bun that has bun:ffi disabled on this platform. That was fixed in Bun 1.4.0 (oven-sh/bun#28055), but the official releases are still built with an older Bun.

So I put together a small pipeline that rebuilds the CLI from the official tag with Bun 1.4.0:

https://github.com/airtaxi/opencode-windows-arm64

It checks for new tags every 6 hours and publishes the win32-arm64 binary along with a Scoop manifest:
```
scoop bucket add opencode-arm64 https://github.com/airtaxi/opencode-windows-arm64
scoop install opencode-arm64
```

Tested on Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme (ASUS Zenbook A16). With Bun 1.4.0 the "TinyCC is disabled" error is gone and the TUI opens fine. The binaries aren't official and aren't signed, but the only change from the official build is the Bun version.

Clarification regarding the possible duplicate #42657:

This V2 report has a different runtime and CPU signature.

- #42657 reports OpenCode V1 (`1.18.18`) with the TUI render thread near 97% CPU, and a follow-up reports 87-100% total CPU across 3-4 OpenCode processes. After restarting with one process, that reporter saw no input lag and peaks below 17%.
- This issue reproduces on OpenCode V2 beta `0.0.0-beta-17793` inside one TUI process with multiple internal virtual tabs. The lag is present while total machine CPU remains around 14%; the shared server was observed around 3.4% of a 32-logical-processor machine. The service remains healthy.

The V2 topology also differs from launching multiple OpenCode processes:

- Internal TUI tabs are views over sessions/workspaces, not separate OS processes.
- In default mode, the TUI connects to one managed background server ([server connection](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/4d22d4e75fb949db5a6302cc605e9af87ea671bf/packages/cli/src/services/server-connection.ts#L21-L50)).
- Session execution is explicitly process-local ([session execution](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/4d22d4e75fb949db5a6302cc605e9af87ea671bf/packages/core/src/session/execution.ts#L17-L54)).
- Subagents are child sessions registered in the process-local Job service, not worker processes ([subagent](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/4d22d4e75fb949db5a6302cc605e9af87ea671bf/packages/core/src/tool/plugin/subagent.ts#L210-L275), [job](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/4d22d4e75fb949db5a6302cc605e9af87ea671bf/packages/core/src/job.ts#L128-L187)).

No worker pool, per-session process placement, or setting that isolates internal TUI tabs was found in this beta. `--standalone` creates one private server for an entire TUI invocation; it does not isolate individual tabs while retaining one TUI.

The directly observed bug remains TUI input/navigation stalls under subagent load. The process-local topology may or may not be the root cause, but it means the V1 multi-process CPU-saturation report should not be assumed to explain this V2 behavior.

Review of `fix(tui): isolate missing-location story data` — nice cleanup overall: replacing the boolean `fixture` prop with an injectable `MoveSessionWorktrees` dependency is a clear improvement over the previous flag-based special-casing, and the new drive simulation test covers the externally-owned-endpoint path end to end. A few points to consider:

- `packages/drive/test/simulation/direct-cli.test.ts:16` — the simulation server binds a hardcoded port `40900`. Any other process holding that port (a dev server, another CI job running in parallel) makes `Bun.serve` throw and fails the suite with an opaque error before any assertion runs. Since testing the CLI's *default* port is presumably intentional, at least catch `EADDRINUSE` at startup and fail/skip with an explicit message naming the conflict, so flakiness is diagnosable instead of mysterious.

- `packages/drive/test/simulation/direct-cli.test.ts:113` — `cwd: resolve(".")` anchors the spawned CLI path to the test runner's current working directory. Under a monorepo vitest invocation from the repo root, `src/cli/index.ts` won't exist relative to that cwd and every spawn fails confusingly. Anchor to the module instead, e.g. `resolve(import.meta.dir, "../../src/cli/index.ts")`, so the test is cwd-independent.

- `packages/drive/test/simulation/direct-cli.test.ts:117` — only `TMPDIR` is overridden in the child env. Windows processes resolve temp directories from `TMP`/`TEMP` and ignore `TMPDIR`, so on Windows CI the child CLI would write temp state outside `root`, defeating the isolation this setup exists for. Set all three (`TMPDIR`, `TMP`, `TEMP`) to `root`.

- `packages/drive/test/simulation/direct-cli.test.ts:25` — `JSON.parse(String(message))` inside the websocket handler has no error handling. A malformed or non-JSON frame throws inside the server callback and surfaces as an unhandled rejection far away from the actual cause. Wrap it in try/catch and reply with a JSON-RPC parse error (`code: -32700`) so bad frames produce a diagnosable response rather than a crashed handler.

- `packages/tui/src/component/dialog-move-session.tsx:30` — `MoveSessionWorktrees.remove` is typed `Promise<unknown>`, but the call sites treat the awaited value as a structured result (`error.data.forceRequired`, passed to `errorMessage`). Typing it `unknown` lets story stubs like `remove: async () => undefined` compile even if they drift from the real contract. Give it a minimal explicit shape (e.g. `Promise<{ error?: unknown } | undefined>`) so the injected fake stays honest about what the component consumes.

- `packages/tui/src/component/dialog-move-session.tsx:79-80` — the resource source now mixes two unrelated skip reasons (`props.current?.type === "directory" || location()?.project.id === props.projectID`). The short-circuit itself looks correct — when a directory-typed `current` is supplied, `currentDirectory()` never reads the lookup result — but nothing on the line says so, and the next reader will wonder why a `current` prop suppresses a project fetch. One sentence of comment (per the repo's "comment non-obvious constraints" guidance) or parentheses around each clause would make the intent obvious.

Minor nit, non-blocking: `packages/drive/test/simulation/direct-cli.test.ts:75-76` asserts exact human-readable stderr substrings ("Unexpected key with value true"); error-copy edits will break CI for no functional reason — matching on exit code plus a stable fragment like `"alt"` alone would be more durable.

Nice work overall — the transactional import (`db.transaction` wrapping session/message/part writes) is a real improvement over the old non-atomic writes, child ordering makes exports deterministic, and the docs are updated. A few concerns:

- `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/import.ts:177-180` (and `:270`) — Strict whole-file validation via `Schema.decodeUnknownExit(SessionTransferFile)` replaces the old lenient per-field decode, and the `time?.created ?? Date.now()` fallback is gone — legacy exports that previously imported (older schemas, missing `time`) now hard-fail with a raw parse error. The test comment at `packages/opencode/test/cli/session-transfer.test.ts:158` acknowledges this tradeoff, but no migration path ships. Suggestion: keep a lenient legacy branch (or version-detect the payload) and/or surface an actionable message like "re-export with a newer opencode" instead of a schema dump.

- `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/import.ts:251-263` — `onConflictDoUpdate` unconditionally repoints any existing session row whose ID collides with an archive entry to the importer's project/directory/path. Importing someone else's shared archive can silently re-home unrelated local sessions (their messages stay due to `onConflictDoNothing`, but ownership metadata is mutated). Suggestion: detect collisions where the existing row differs and require an explicit opt-in flag, or skip with a warning listing the affected IDs.

- `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/import.ts:232-245` — The strand check only inspects *direct children of moved* sessions, so an archive that includes a child but omits its parent passes validation: the child moves to the target project while its parent stays behind, splitting the tree across projects. `collectSessionTree` always emits complete subtrees, but hand-edited or partially trimmed archives validate fine. Suggestion: additionally require each included session's `parentID` to be either included in the archive or already resident in the target project.

- `packages/opencode/test/cli/session-transfer.test.ts:105-157` — Tests cover the deep round-trip and the legacy-rejection path (`:159-182`), but there is no test that a plain legacy `{info, messages}` single-session file still imports successfully through the new union decode. That's the main backward-compatibility contract of this change; suggestion: add a happy-path legacy import test asserting rows land in the target project.

- `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/import.ts:298` — Converting `SqlError` to a defect via `Effect.die` turns ordinary DB failures (locked database, constraint violation, disk full) into crashes with stack traces rather than a friendly CLI error. Suggestion: `fail` with a formatted message, consistent with the other import errors in this file.

- `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/export.ts:15-24` — Cycle/duplicate protection in `collectSessionTree` depends on `seen` being mutated between sibling visits, which only holds because `Effect.forEach` defaults to sequential concurrency; a future switch to concurrent traversal would silently reintroduce duplicate visits. Suggestion: add a comment documenting the sequential-traversal invariant (or dedupe after collection).

- `packages/tui/src/feature-plugins/system/plugins.tsx:67-72` — The toggle computes the desired state from the runtime snapshot (`!current.active`) instead of from the config draft it is about to mutate — If config and runtime ever diverge (external edit to `opencode.json`, an in-flight reconcile, or a previous toggle whose apply failed), clicking toggle can re-enable a plugin the user explicitly disabled (or vice versa) — the exact class of bug this PR sets out to fix. Suggestion: derive the effective state inside the update callback, e.g. check whether `draft.plugins` currently contains `id` or `` `-${id}` `` (absence = enabled) and flip that, so the decision is made against the same data being written.
- `packages/tui/src/feature-plugins/system/plugins.tsx:74-79` — The soft-failure signal is gone: the old code showed a "Failed to update plugin …" toast when `activate`/`deactivate` returned `false`, but the new path treats any resolved `config.update` as success — a validation rejection or silent no-op write leaves the user with no feedback while the option footer keeps showing the stale active/inactive state. Suggestion: verify the resulting config (return value or a follow-up `config.get()`) contains the expected directive, and fall back to the error toast when it did not land.

Update: identified the precise trigger for why this suddenly surfaced.

We run LiteLLM as the proxy in front of Bedrock Mantle and had been silently unaffected by this OpenCode bug for months because **LiteLLM itself was silently dropping the `verbosity` param** before v1.92.0 — `completion()`/`acompletion()` omitted `verbosity` from the kwargs passed to `get_optional_params()`, so it never reached the provider at all (fixed upstream in [BerriAI/litellm#32254](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/32254)).

We upgraded our proxy from LiteLLM v1.91.0 → v1.97.0, which includes that fix. Now that LiteLLM correctly forwards `verbosity` downstream, Bedrock Mantle's rejection of the parameter is exposed, and every `gpt-5.x` request through our `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` provider fails with `UnsupportedParamsError`.

So: this is not a new bug in OpenCode, and not a regression from a recent OpenCode release — it's a latent bug (present since at least January 2026, per `transform.ts` git history) that was accidentally masked by an unrelated LiteLLM bug, and is now surfaced by LiteLLM fixing their side. The fix in #43915 is still correct and still needed — OpenCode shouldn't unconditionally send `verbosity` to providers that don't support it regardless of what any given proxy version happens to do with it.
